newsitem.title: POLAND: Kredyt Bank seen buoyed by PBI purchase.
newsitem.headline: Kredyt Bank seen buoyed by PBI purchase.

text.p: Poland's Kredyt Bank SA is seen profiting by the end of the decade from its Friday agreement to buy Polish Investment Bank (PBI) and Prosper Bank, but analysts said short-term financing questions still needed answering.
On Friday Kredyt agreed to buy from the central bank all of PBI and 92.36 percent of ailing Prosper for 205 million zlotys and invest about another 290 million zlotys in the two banks.
Kredyt has said it would merge with PBI and later with Prosper when it is restructured, boosting its branch network and client base, to form the country's eighth largest bank.
Analysts on Monday said the long-term earnings benefits of the deal would likely be discounted by the market in the short- and medium- term despite today's question marks on financing.
"I would think the market would probably react that big is better," said Denise Vergot Holle, financial institutions analyst at Merrill Lynch in London.
Kredyt Bank rose 3.7 percent on Friday, when news of the agreement broke, and jumped 6.5 percent on Monday in a positive bourse session when seven stocks rose above nine percent.
But financing questions remain, analysts said.

"They might need to take out some loans to cover their operating activities...Prosper's 160 million zlotys in losses is a lot to swallow, and Kredyt is still interested in buying some of (bank) PBK," said Tomasz Cwintal of BGZ brokerage.
PBI made a 55.2-million-zloty net profit in 1996 and ended the year with a capital of 197.1 million zlotys.

Kredyt Bank ended 1996 with capital of 219 million zlotys, Prosper of 16.1 million zlotys. At the end of last year Kredyt, PBI and Prosper had balance sheet totals of 1.07 billion, 4.56 billion and 557 million zlotys respectively.
Merrill's Holle said the purchase of PBI and Prosper might force Kredyt to limit its desired share in privatising PBK, or Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA, to as low as five percent.

Kredyt, BPH, PBR and insurer Warta seek to form a banking-insurance group with PBK, 65 percent of which the finance ministry plans to sell by the end of April to a foreign or domestic strategic investor.
A public offering of 15 percent of shares is due around October.

Kredyt has said it would use its own funds to buy PBI and Prosper as well as funds from an upcoming issue of 10 million shares at eight zlotys each. It will also offer 847,000 shares to the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).

BGZ's Cwintal said that though Kredyt Bank shares could fall with the overall market should the latter hit a downtrend, the stock, currently at 9.05 zlotys, could reach 15 zlotys in one and a half to two years.
Many analysts see the Warsaw bourse stabilising at best at mid-year due to a batch of large initial public offerings and parliamentary elections due around September.
